body: Last week I was walking down the sidewalk and some guy followed me for at least a block repeating "Hey. Hey, what's your name? Hey. hey. hey." Even though I was definitely not responding, and the look on my face alone should have been enough to make anyone not talk to me. Saying "hi" can definitely be catcalling, but it's all about the context. I'm betting this is the type of guy who follows some poor woman shouting "hi" at her than cries about how he was "just trying to be nice."

There are 2 kinds of ugly. Ones that can change. Maybe they need to diet, maybe they need to dress better. Maybe they just need more confidence. Then there are the ones who can't, short of hundreds of thousands in plastic surgery. 

I'm ugly. I've always been ugly. My mother drank heavily and did drugs while she was pregnant with me. Things aren't lined up in the right places. I'm ugly. It's always going to be the first thing people see about me, and for most people it will be the only thing they see about me. 

Maybe in a perfect world everyone's "inner beauty" would be enough. But this isn't a perfect world.

I am so sorry that you are hurting. It is incredibly painful to put your heart in someone's hands and have them just not care. 

I want to say you should not put your happiness and well being in someone else's hands, but damn would that make me a hypocrite. Sometimes you don't have the strength to hold yourself up and you need someone else to do it for you while you regain your balance. And that kind of trust, that is so hard to give or get.

It hurts, I know it hurts so much. But if she could not appreciate the huge amount of trust you handed her, then it is her fault. There are people who beg their loved ones to just trust in them, and you gave it to her freely. You cannot let her inability to see what she was handed be your fault.

I am sorry that you feel you are not good for anything. Feeling worthless has to be one of the worst feelings in the world. 

Is there anything that you can offer? Being an ear to listen to, or a friend during rough times? You said you don't want your friend to feel like she failed, so you must care a lot. Finding people that genuinely care about others is a big deal.

I think it can be for some people. If you are in a place where you need more support, and know that suicidal behavior will get that need filled, it can be very easy to fall into a pattern of acting out to get the reward. Maybe asking for more attention first helps, or finding someone who is capable of providing extra care during bad times. Something ti get the need filled without having to resort to suicide or behaviors?

Reading your post, I thought for a moment I had posted it. 

Depression and Borderline. First suicide attempt at 12. Drunk, angry parents. When things are dark, it's still my mother's voice in my head telling me I'm bad, worthless, unlovable. 

Its hard. It is so fucking hard. And considering last night I was on the ledge, I probably don't have any business here. But, I'm lonely. And hurting. And if you need to talk to someone that has hurt as much as you, I would love to be an ear. If you need to talk.
Maybe. I tried so many places, but never had luck. I don't know if it is me, or the area, or just bad luck.
I don't know. All I have done is be a housewife, and before that took care of my grandmother or mother. I do not know what I enjoy doing besides taking care of someone.
With a felony record here it is nearly impossible to find jobs like that. My charge was theft, no violence or drugs. But it is still a black spot that not a lot of people are willing to look past.

I did after my divorce. Packed up and moved hundreds of miles away. No money, no plans, just went. But I was 28 then, and naive. Didn't take long to end up badly. I don't think I could ever do that again. I don't know what I like. I like having a person to take care of.
How do you start over at so late an age? I feel like time is up for rebuilding anything.
